title: Psalm 127: Unless the LORD Builds the House
summary: Building a house, guarding a city, and working from dawn to late at night are all in vain unless the LORD is the one building and guarding, for he gives sleep to those he loves. Children, the psalm continues, are a heritage and reward from the LORD, like arrows in a warrior's hand, and a man with many of them will not be put to shame when he faces his opponents at the city gate.

line: Building and guarding are in vain unless the LORD builds and guards; he gives sleep to those he loves, and children are a heritage from him.
guide: Work without God is in vain, and worry is not the same as work; lying down to rest can be an act of trust. If you have children, hold them as gifts in trust, arrows made to be sent out. The psalm's praise of children is no promise of a child to everyone who prays for one.

care.text: A word of care. Verses 3 to 5 praise children as God's gift. They do not promise a child to everyone who prays for one, and a gift is not a wage. Many faithful people long for children and never have them, or lose them before birth. Childlessness is not a judgment from God, and it does not measure your faith. Your longing is seen. If the grief is heavy, please share it with someone you trust: a friend, a pastor, a counsellor.

A home without children, or a single person, is not less blessed in God's eyes. Jesus himself lived and died without wife or children. The family of God is wider than any one household, and there is a place in it for you.

stanzas.title: Unless the LORD builds and guards
Anxious toil is in vain; the LORD gives sleep
Children as a heritage, arrows, and a full quiver

verses.t: A song of ascents. Of Solomon. Unless the LORD builds the house, its builders labor in vain; unless the LORD protects the city, its watchmen stand guard in vain.
In vain you rise early and stay up late, toiling for bread to eat— for He gives sleep to His beloved.
Children are indeed a heritage from the LORD, and the fruit of the womb is His reward.
Like arrows in the hand of a warrior, so are children born in one’s youth.
Blessed is the man whose quiver is full of them. He will not be put to shame when he confronts the enemies at the gate.
